pl-l4d45c3-d1e121.summary: Quotes Augustine: funeral pomp, processions, and costly burial are consolations of the living, not help for the dead; if a precious burial helped the impious, a poor or none would harm the pious; the purple-clad rich man had a splendid funeral from his servants, but the ulcerous poor man had a far more splendid one from angels, who carried him not to a marble tomb but to Abraham's bosom.
claims: Costly burial does not help the dead.

pl-l4d45c3-d1e127.summary: Continues: yet care for burying the dead and building tombs should be kept, since Scripture counts these good works and praises those who did them for the patriarchs and the Lord's body; let people fulfill these last duties and consolations of grief, but more diligently provide offerings and prayers, which help the spirits of the dead.
claims: Prayers and offerings help the dead more.

pl-l4d45c3.summary: On funeral pomp, Augustine says that processions and costly burial console the living but do not help the dead; a precious burial does not help the impious nor a poor one harm the pious, as the rich man had a grand funeral while angels carried Lazarus to Abraham's bosom. Still, burying the dead is praised in Scripture as a good work, as for the patriarchs and the Lord's body, but offerings and prayers, which help the dead, should be more diligently provided.
claims: Funeral pomp consoles the living but does not help the dead.
Burying the dead is a praiseworthy work.
Prayers and offerings matter more than funerals.
